title: Scientists Find ‘Chorus Waves’ in Unexpected Part of Space
speaker: VOA Learning English

sentences.en: Scientists call the energetic activity “ chorus waves” because they are said to move at the same frequency as sounds humans can hear.
sentences.zh: 科学家称活跃的活动为“合唱波”,因为据说它们以与人类听到的声音相同的频率移动。

sentences.en: When the energy is turned into audio signals, the waves sound like birds chirping .
sentences.zh: 当能量变成音频信号时 海浪听起来就像鸟儿的鸣叫

sentences.en: Researchers have known about chorus waves in space for many years.
sentences.zh: 研究人员多年来一直了解空间的合唱波。

sentences.en: But the latest research has found the waves exist 100,000 kilometers from Earth.
sentences.zh: 但最新的研究发现 海浪存在于离地球10万公里之外

sentences.en: Chorus waves have never before been measured at such a big distance from a planet.
sentences.zh: 和声波从未被测量到 距离地球如此之远

sentences.en: In an email, study writer Chengming Liu from Beihang University in Beijing wrote: “They are one of the strongest and most significant waves in space.”
sentences.zh: 北京北京大学的研究作家刘成明在一封电子邮件中写道 : “ 它们是空间中最强大和最重要的浪潮之一。 ”

sentences.en: Allison Jaynes is a space physicist at the University of Iowa who was not involved with the study.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森·杰恩斯是爱荷华大学的一名空间物理学家 他没有参与研究

sentences.en: Speaking about the recent study, Jaynes said, “That opens up a lot of new questions about the physics that could be possible in this area.” The newfound chorus waves were detected in an area where Earth's magnetic field is stretched out.
sentences.zh: 谈到最近的研究,Jaynes说, “ 这打开了许多关于物理学的新问题,而在这一领域是可能的。 ”新发现的合唱波是在地球磁场伸展的地区探测到的。

sentences.en: Scientists said they did not expect to find the waves there.
sentences.zh: 科学家们说,他们并不期望在那里发现海浪。

sentences.en: The discovery raises new questions about how the chirping waves form.
sentences.zh: 这一发现提出了关于声波如何形成的新问题。

sentences.en: Jaynes added, “We definitely need to find more of these events.” Scientists still are not sure how the waves develop.
sentences.zh: Jaynes补充说, “ 我们绝对需要找到更多这些事件。 ”科学家们仍然不确定波浪是如何发展的。

sentences.en: But they think Earth’s magnetic field may have something to do with it.
sentences.zh: 但他们认为地球的磁场可能与它有关。

sentences.en: For many years, radio antennas have picked up chorus waves.
sentences.zh: 多年来,无线电天线接收到合唱波。

sentences.en: This includes receivers at an Antarctica research station in the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 这包括1960年代南极研究站的接收器。

sentences.en: And NASA’s two Van Allen Probes heard the chirping sounds from Earth's radiation belts at a closer distance than the newest observations.
sentences.zh: 美国航天局的两个Van Allen Probes 听到地球辐射带的鸣叫声,距离比最新的观测更近。

sentences.en: The latest chorus waves were picked up by NASA's Magnetospheric Multiscale satellites.
sentences.zh: 美国航天局的磁层多级卫星接收了最新的合唱波。

sentences.en: They were launched in 2015 to explore the Earth and the sun's magnetic fields.
sentences.zh: 它们于2015年发射,用于探索地球和太阳的磁场。

sentences.en: Chorus waves have also been found near other planets including Jupiter and Saturn.
sentences.zh: 在木星和土星等其他行星附近也发现了合唱波。

sentences.en: The waves can produce high-energy electrons.
sentences.zh: 海浪可以产生高能电子。

sentences.en: That means they can threaten satellite communications.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它们可以威胁卫星通信。

sentences.en: The researchers said their findings suggest that chorus waves might be found everywhere in the magnetic fields of planets.
sentences.zh: 研究人员说,他们的研究结果表明,在行星的磁场中,到处都能找到合唱波。

sentences.en: The study was released on January 22 in the scientific publication Nature .
sentences.zh: 研究于1月22日在科学出版物《自然》中发布。

sentences.en: I’m Anna Matteo. Adithi Ramakrishnan reported this story for the Associated Press from New York.
sentences.zh: 我是Anna Matteo, Adithi Ramakrishnan 在纽约为美联社报导此事。

sentences.en: Anna Matteo adapted it for VOA Learning English.
sentences.zh: Anna Matteo改编成VOA英文学习版。
